questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted somewhere in europe. Something that was neather too similar to Denmark but also not too different. Good univerisity with good courses.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: They send mails with info and some info was on canvas, but it was were easy to miss something, so good idea to talk to other people.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I didn't recieve any

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found it through the university. I would recommend that because otherwise it is very difficult to find anything and also very expensive. You have to pay 250€ to be able to apply but if you are ready when they open for the housing registration, you can defininetly get something.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I lived in Uilenstede which is a area with only student housing so good oppotunities to meet other people. It is a bit further from the central part of Amsterdam, but it is possible to bike there or take the traim.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: There was a lot of different thing to register. I had to apply for preapproval of the couses which was very difficult and recuired a lot of emails and sending different documents.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There where different people you could contact.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I did get the classes that I wanted. However it was not very easy. I could not register through the normal registration process and had to send a bunch of mails and documents to different people.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Write down the different deadlines and make sure you meet them. If there are couses you can't find in the normal registration form write to them because it might be a mistake or you have to apply another way to get them.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Think they required that you have 90 ECTS in relevant studies. We had many lectures (2-4 hours a day typically, and one thay off) so there was a lot of information, but also a lot of repetition. Other students in the class have already had immunology which made it a little bit more difficult if you have not had it, but it is manageable and not too hardcore.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Only lectures no other classes so a bit repetitative.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Minor in Cancer-Immune Disease-Personalized Therapy

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I think it was a good course and that I learned something. However, it was intendend for medical studients so some was a bit irrelevant.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Had to pay 250€ to register for housing. Had to buy a lot of things that was missing e.g. kitchen items, stuff for the apartment, etc.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food is a bit less expesive. Housing is very expesive if you don't get student housing.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were different clubs that you could joint. They did intro days with many different activities/parties that you could sign up for. You could sign up for Sportcenter/fitness.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Sign up for all of the stuff in the intro-days. It is a good way to meet people.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to the city, see the markeds, visit other nearby towns, go to the lake to swim in the sommer, go to nearby countries.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy as it is very similar.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I lived in a building with sheared kitchen which made it easier to meet people. Also sign up for the activities in the introdays.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not really

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: There was always life in the city even when the weather was bad.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
You meet a lot of other exchange students from many different cultures.
They academic levels is decent.
They city is soo nice and many good areas when you get to know it a little.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you want something not too different from Copenhagen culture but still very nice and with the oppotunity to meet a lot of new people, I would recomend it.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting so many different people and become more comfortable making conversation with people you don't know.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I did miss my home a bit.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
